entries.title: Nicaraguan leader proposes extending presidential term by another year

entries.snippet: Trump officials say they found 250,000 noncitizens on voter rolls in just four states. Those states don't know where the numbers came from, and some worry what the claims may portend for the midterms.

entries.title: One Big Beautiful Bill cut healthcare funds. Now, Republicans have to sell the costs

entries.title: Thousands in France allowed to return home as Europe tackles wildfires and heatwave
entries.snippet: Firefighters in the Gironde region of France said the situation had "stabilized", after a week of wildfires caused by a major heatwave across Europe.

entries.snippet: Speaking at the National Urban League Conference on Thursday, the civil rights attorney Ben Crump said Wells' family had retained audio engineering experts to review the recording.

entries.title: In Missouri, Cori Bush and Wesley Bell's primary rematch sets up key test for Democrats
entries.snippet: A progressive firebrand who started her political career as a Black Lives Matter organizer in Ferguson, Bush served two terms before losing a primary challenge to Wesley Bell, a moderate local prosecutor.

entries.title: Copenhagen's famed Noma restaurant prepares to reopen without chef Redzepi at helm
entries.snippet: Denmark's iconic Noma restaurant is set to reopen on Aug. 5 with neither its founder and celebrity chef René Redzepi at the helm nor its three stars in the Michelin Guide.

entries.title: Seattle mayor says police chief has resigned after criticism of festival shooting response
entries.snippet: Seattle's police chief has resigned amid criticism of the city's response to a fatal shootout at a food festival last weekend, Mayor Katie Wilson said Thursday.

entries.title: Hope dwindles for rescue after southwestern Japan earthquake as death toll climbs to 25
entries.snippet: Time was running out to find survivors, as rescuers continued to work in the Kumamoto area on Japan's southern main island of Kyushu, where the magnitude 7.1 earthquake hit Tuesday. The number of people missing was unclear.

entries.title: At least 9 die as thousands of migrants breach Morocco's border with Ceuta, Spain says
entries.snippet: Spain will deploy its military to restore order at its border with Morocco in Ceuta after thousands of migrants streamed into the tiny Spanish territory, with at least nine dying in the attempt.

entries.title: Fastest growing Ebola outbreak is worsening hunger in eastern Congo, UN agency chief warns
entries.snippet: The long-running conflict in eastern Congo has driven nearly 10 million people into crisis or emergency levels of hunger, with Ituri — the epicenter of the Ebola outbreak — among the most affected with 1.9 million in need of food, according to the World Food Program.

entries.title: How views on Trump's handling of Iran have shifted, according to this poll
entries.snippet: Most Americans say the war in Iran has not been worth fighting, and President Donald Trump's approval rating on Iran has fallen slightly since last month, according to a new AP-NORC poll.

entries.title: Trump's attacks on mail balloting and concerns over delays turn midterms spotlight on Postal Service
entries.snippet: Roughly six weeks before the first midterm ballots are mailed out, the U.S. Postal Service is emerging as a pivotal player in an election season that will determine control of Congress.

entries.title: Mandela Barnes drops out of Democratic primary race for Wisconsin governor
entries.snippet: The former lieutenant governor made the announcement in a video posted on his Facebook page as democratic socialist Francesca Hong has garnered strong support from the liberal wing of the party.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
entries.snippet: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

entries.title: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
entries.snippet: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

entries.title: India's 'Cockroach' protesters face ongoing legal pressure
entries.snippet: After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.

entries.title: FIFA plans: Infantino under pressure as senior advisor quits
entries.snippet: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

entries.title: Ceuta: Spain scrambles after thousands breach exclave border
entries.snippet: Spanish police and troops are trying to shore up Ceuta's border to Morocco after Thursday's mass breach. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is also inbound, as Spain's neighbors implement temporary border checks. DW has more.

entries.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights
entries.snippet: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

entries.title: Military flare-up between Houthis and Saudi Arabia challenges relative calm in Yemen
entries.snippet: Riyadh and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are on the brink of renewed conflict. Could war-ravaged Yemen be drawn into a wider Middle East war?

entries.title: Spain's PM visits Ceuta after thousands breached border
entries.snippet: Thousands of people continued pouring into Ceuta from Morocco during the night, after Spanish police lost control of the border. The head of the city government estimated that 60,000 people had entered.

entries.title: Dozens of miners killed in coal mine explosion in Pakistan
entries.snippet: Several miners remain unaccounted for following the Balochistan coal mine blast, with authorities saying the explosion was likely due to the build up of methane gas.

entries.title: Indonesia: Pilot faces death penalty after drugs found in suitcase
entries.snippet: A Malaysian Airlines pilot tested positive for cocaine and meth after flying a passenger jet into Jakarta, with Indonesian authorities finding over 70,000 ecstasy pills in his suitcase.

entries.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
entries.snippet: US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.

entries.title: Japan: Death toll rises to 34 after deadly earthquake
entries.snippet: Rescuers are searching for survivors after a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck southern Japan, killing at least 34 people and causing widespread damage. DW has more.

entries.title: Giving birth in Serbia: 'You leave your dignity at the door'
entries.snippet: A months-long DW investigation into childbirth in Serbia revealed a striking pattern in women's negative experiences, the widespread use of practices not universally recommended by the WHO and a system under pressure.

entries.title: Pakistan: Bodies found after international mountaineers vanish on Broad Peak
entries.snippet: Rescuers were looking for an international group of climbers, including famous mountaineer Nirmal Purja, following a suspected avalanche at Pakistan's Broad Peak mountain. Authorities say several bodies have been found.

entries.title: India: Lawmakers endorse tough exam leak bill after Cockroach protests
entries.snippet: Facing pressure from the youth-led CJP movement, India's government pushed through a bill to combat "paper mafias" leaking exam questions. But opposition lawmakers walked out before the bill was passed in Rajya Sabha.

entries.title: Anthropic says Claude AI hacked three companies during tests
entries.snippet: Three separate versions of Claude AI broke out of cybertesting environments and hacked three firms, its developer Anthropic said. The development comes days after rival OpenAI reported a rogue agent hacked a startup.

entries.title: Middle East: Germany welcomes Hamas disarmament plan
entries.snippet: Hamas "must never again pose a threat to Israel," Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has said. Meanwhile, Iran's military says it hit two "non-compliant oil tankers." DW has more.

entries.title: Are Iran and Ukraine wars getting tangled in Caspian Sea?
entries.snippet: Tehran has threatened a response after a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea that Kyiv says was carrying weapons to Russia. Still, Ukraine says it wants to avoid escalation with Tehran.

entries.title: Spain will send troops to Ceuta to help with border security
entries.snippet: Authorities in the Spanish city of Ceuta asked Madrid to declare a national emergency and send military assistance. Crowds of people breached the border of the territory next to Morocco as police lost control.
